- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.23) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >82), model often overcorrects downward; delay or dampen the correction to allow for mean reversion.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.16) over 3–5 days, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.0 to forecast to counteract pessimism.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative — adjust upward by 0.3–0.8.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often lags behind true trend by 1–2 days; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead if sentiment is trending upward.
- If sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model may miss the momentum — increase forecast slope or add 0.5–1.0 to latest 3–5 day average.
